page.layout: One printed page, one column of text, centred. From top to bottom: a woodcut ornamental border; a heading in italic; a verse poem of a large initial stanza and short lines; a dedication line in italic with a signature in capitals; the word FINIS in spaced capitals; a woodcut ornament at the foot. No marginal notes. Faint show-through from the reverse page is not transcribed.

main_text.head: Ornatissimo Dn. Respondenti.
main_text.p: SCANDIT in excelsam populo spectante cathedram DE LOSEA, sumos appetit atq; gradus. Plaudite Sicelides, gratantia fundite vota, Inq; caput flores spargite odoriferos. Nunc vigilando tibi palmam laurumq; parasti, Quæ magni semper signa laboris erunt. Horrendum David membris animisq; Goliam, Hostes, ut vicit, sic superare queas.
Hæc paucula cognato suo perdilecto scripsit CORNELIUS SUTER.
main_text.head: FINIS

page.notes: The initial S of the poem is a large decorative letter, joined to "CANDIT". The first word of the poem is set in small capitals. Ornamental woodcuts above and below the text are not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "gratantia" and "Goliam" are as printed. Verse lines are kept as printed, with long s replaced by s.
